problems.quote:
The same line also clears the key mapping (`KeyMapping.set(key, false)`), so whatever you have M bound to does
not fire alongside it.
problems.issue: Misattributed to "the same line". Neither quoted line calls KeyMapping.set. In KeyboardHandler.keyPress the clearing happens in a separate branch further down: `if (flag4) { if (flag5) { KeyMapping.set(inputconstants$key, false); } else { KeyMapping.set(inputconstants$key, true); KeyMapping.click(inputconstants$key); } }` — gated on the same `flag5`, but additionally on `flag4` (screen == null), and it passes the `InputConstants.Key` object, not the int `key`. The practical consequence the sentence draws (your M binding does not also fire) is correct.
problems.correction: "The same `flag5` is read again further down in `keyPress`: when it is set and no screen is open, vanilla calls `KeyMapping.set(inputconstants$key, false)` instead of `set(..., true)` + `click(...)`, so whatever you have M bound to does not fire alongside it."

problems.issue: Overstated. Re-enabling the module (config key `enabled` or the runtime override, which `ModuleManager.resolveModuleEnabled` honours on every call) makes the mixin's `isActiveClientSide()` gate pass again, and one F3+M then calls `SpawnOverlayState.toggle()`, which sets `markers = List.of()`. A restart is not the only way out of the stale-marker state.
problems.correction: "They stay until you re-enable the module and toggle the overlay off again — or restart."

problems.issue: SOURCE BUG (SpawnOverlayRenderer.java:64-67, not a doc-writing error) — the renderer takes three VertexConsumers from the same `MultiBufferSource.BufferSource` up front and then writes to all three inside the marker loop. None of the six custom RenderTypes is in `RenderBuffers`' `fixedBuffers` map (the mod never subscribes to `RegisterRenderBuffersEvent` — grep over src/ finds no reference), so all three land on the *shared* ByteBufferBuilder. `MultiBufferSource.BufferSource.getBuffer` (1.21.1, decompiled) runs `if (this.lastSharedType != null) this.endBatch(this.lastSharedType);` before creating the next shared builder, and `endBatch` calls `builder.build()`, which sets `building = false`. So fetching `shimmer` kills `stripes`, fetching `outline` kills `shimmer`; the first `quad(stripes, …)` then hits `BufferBuilder.addVertex` → `beginVertex()` → `ensureBuilding()` → `throw new IllegalStateException("Not building!")` inside RenderLevelStageEvent, i.e. a client crash as soon as the overlay is on with at least one marker. The same pattern sits in ChunkLoaderBorderRenderer.java:80-81, AnchorBorderRenderer.java:58-59 and ChunkLoaderTrackBorderRenderer.java:91-92; BattleDogsArmorLayer.java:59/65 shows the correct sequential get-use-get-use shape. I could not run the game to observe the crash, and no log or crash report in ~/.minecraft-instances mentions the module, so this is read off vanilla's source — but it is the one finding worth acting on. If it is real, the page's user-visible promises ("every position … lights up", the shimmer, the outline) describe intent rather than observed behaviour.
problems.correction: Not a page fix. In the code: fetch each VertexConsumer immediately before writing to it (or give the six types their own buffers via `RegisterRenderBuffersEvent`), then verify in-game before the page keeps asserting the overlay draws.

problems.quote: the light test itself, evaluated against the dimension's {@link IntProvider} range rather
problems.issue: WRONG COMMENT (SpawnScanner.java:24-34, not a doc error) — the class javadoc lists the per-position checks "in order of cost" as 1 block light, 2 ON_GROUND placement, 3 collision, 4 the light test. The code runs the light test SECOND (`localBrightness > everDarkEnough → continue`, lines 81-84), before `fits(...)` does the placement and collision tests. The doc page describes the real order (block light → ever dark enough → ground → hitbox) and is right where the javadoc is not.
problems.correction: Leave the page as it is; reorder items 2-4 of the SpawnScanner javadoc to match the code.
